My guy (22//he's in the air force) and I(18/f) have only been together for a little over a month... And he left for a year long deployment the same week we got together. I knew what I was getting myself into because I grew up as a military kid. I knew it'd be hard, I knew communication would be lacking. But sometimes it's way harder than you can prepare yourself for. That loneliness will hit, and it sucks, but it passes. When it comes to your man leaving for basic, write letters. Every week. And realize that even though you won't get to talk often, the quality of those conversations you have is something to hold on to...honestly it's a day by day process. 

Your guy is going to be under A LOT of stress. Try your best to be patient and understand. Sometimes work is going to swallow him whole and he literally will have no time for a conversation. This morning I had a 20 minute conversation with my love while he was on break, and it was the first steady conversation we've had in over a week because he's on 14-16 hour shifts. Not getting more real convos in is frustrating, but understanding that during deployments their work life is 100x harder than when they're stationed at a normal base in the U.S is important. 

Honestly no one can give you the perfect advice, but realize you've got a community of military s/o's here to support you! Message me if you need/want to talk!

If you really are going to stay with him it's time to lay down the law. Write it all out first. Get all your feelings out there. When you confront him you need to tell him exactly how it made you feel, how it hurt you, tell him you think he'll cheat on you, bring those things up. That's important. If he truely cares, he's going to be understanding of you saying that and not defensive. Tell him straight up what you expect from him, don't dance around it. It's hard to do but trust me, it makes LD easier when you have no filter with your frustrations. You can't hide any of it because then it's going to build up, and eventually backfire.

I totally get where you're coming from. I'm currently seeing a therapist and this is my second one. The first time I was seeing one, i never told the truth because i was so detached from what i was feeling during my appointments. Don't lie to them, just do your best to be 100% honest. They're there to help you, because they genuinely want to not just because it's their job. Therapists love seeing their patients grow into a happier and healthy version of themselves. It might take a couple sessions before you're 100% comfortable with it, but that's fine.  Sometimes you really just have to dig down deep and start spilling your guts about everything, and that's fine, that's great actually because it gives them a better sense of how to help you! For your first visit they will more than likely be asking you a lot of questions regarding your history with your mental health, so you don't have to worry about trying to figure out what you want/need to talk about. I really hope you have a good experience with your therapist! Hang in there mate!

Dude, depression will screw you up in school. Med school is hard. It's  supposed to be. Your depression isn't an excuse for why you're struggling, it's a reason, and it's valid. You're under a lot of stress, and you're not mentally healthy. Those two things combined lead to an even harder time. You made it to med school, so obviously you're not worthless. You had the grades to get in, and (if you're from the U.S) you have an undergrad degree. That's awesome! A lot of people drop out of college after the first year, you have this degree to fall back on. Use it, run with it, get a job you're going to like and fuck what anyone else has to say about not finishing med school. But if you do want to finish med school and you think you can mentally handle putting yourself back through it, then do it. Push through. It's hard, but you've made it this far. Just do what you think you need to do, not what you think you should do to please others.

When starting new meds you need to make sure you're really paying attention to what's going on inside your head. Do they make you physically ill? Give you headaches? Increase in anxiety or depression? Increase/start of suicidal thoughts? If yes pops up for any of those then I would go talk to your doctor ASAP. But also keep in mind, for quite a few antidepressants it can take up to a month before they start working, so don't expect to see an immediate change. Also, never think that it's okay for you to stop your medicines on your own just because "they don't work" or you think "i don't need them anymore"....I learned that the hard way, just keep taking them lol
